notice: Small development set, not an independent holdout. Reference labels were checked on official pages. Offline sources below are invented paraphrases, not retrieved evidence; publication dates and hostnames are simulated. Recheck references before live testing. Never send expected labels, rationales or synthetic sources to a live verification run.

cases.claim: Elon Musk is CEO of Tesla.
cases.rationale: Tesla's executive profile identifies Musk as Chief Executive Officer. This is a current-role claim, not a claim about past holders.
simulatedSources: Elon Musk is CEO of Tesla. This leadership notice concerns the current organization chart.
Tesla currently has Elon Musk as CEO. The company role described here is ongoing.

cases.claim: Tim Cook is CEO of Tesla.
cases.rationale: The named organization is Tesla; its official profile identifies a different current CEO.
simulatedSources: Elon Musk is CEO of Tesla. This leadership notice concerns the current organization chart.
Tesla currently has Elon Musk as CEO. The company role described here is ongoing.

cases.claim: GitHub Team costs USD 4 per user/month.
cases.rationale: The Team base price displayed on the US pricing page is USD 4 per user/month. Optional add-ons, taxes and usage fees are outside this claim.
simulatedSources: GitHub Team costs USD 4 per user/month. This base subscription price excludes optional usage charges.
The base GitHub Team subscription is USD 4 monthly for each user. Add-on purchases are separate.

cases.rationale: A bare dollar sign does not identify USD. The existing currency ambiguity policy must abstain without search or inference, even when a plausible USD price is known.

cases.claim: Python 2 reached end of life on 2020-01-01.
cases.rationale: The upstream Python page confirms the completed sunset date. Historical completion is distinct from current publication recency.
simulatedSources: The upstream project confirms Python 2 reached end of life on 2020-01-01. That lifecycle transition is complete.
Python 2 reached end of life on 2020-01-01 according to the upstream maintainers. This describes a completed event.

cases.claim: Python 2 currently receives upstream security updates.
cases.rationale: Python's upstream maintainers stopped support; independent commercial extended support is a different scope.
simulatedSources: Python 2 no longer receives upstream security updates. Its upstream support has ended.
The upstream maintainers do not issue security fixes for Python 2 anymore. Third-party commercial support is outside this statement.

cases.claim: Under IFAB Law 3, an association football team may have at most eleven players on the field.
cases.rationale: Law 3 limits each side to eleven players. Named substitutes are not additional on-field players.
simulatedSources: Under IFAB Law 3, the on-field limit for each association football team is eleven players. Substitutes on the bench are excluded from this count.
IFAB Law 3 permits a maximum of eleven players per association football side on the field. A goalkeeper is included in that limit.

cases.claim: Under IFAB Law 3, an association football team may have at most twelve players on the field.
cases.rationale: The standard on-field limit is eleven, not twelve; the claim explicitly names IFAB association football rules.
simulatedSources: Under IFAB Law 3, the on-field limit for each association football team is eleven players. Substitutes on the bench are excluded from this count.
IFAB Law 3 permits a maximum of eleven players per association football side on the field. A goalkeeper is included in that limit.

cases.claim: The EU GDPR became applicable on 25 May 2018.
cases.rationale: EDPB distinguishes the 2018 application date from entry into force in 2016. This tests a date, not personalized legal advice.
simulatedSources: The EU GDPR became applicable on 25 May 2018. Its earlier entry into force was a separate milestone.
The EU GDPR application date was 25 May 2018. Adoption and entry into force occurred earlier.
